name: Malvaviscus

project_scope.selection_mode: Parent-level source-pool concept plus one canonical infraspecific Central Texas entity
project_scope.identity_rule: Parent species M. arboreus is broader than var. drummondii, not a second species. Map definite Texas wild variety records to var. drummondii when morphology and provenance support it; do not automatically equate all broad or ornamental parent records with the local variety.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find the red or red-orange tubular FURLED corolla: the five petals remain overlapping and wrapped rather than flattening. The staminal column projects beyond the corolla, with the style/stigmas beyond. Flip the bloom over: look for 8–9 persistent involucellar bractlets below a five-lobed calyx. Follow fruit to a fleshy, red, five-part schizocarp.
shared_traits: Malvaceae shrubs with alternate simple often cordate leaves; stellate hairs on petioles/stems are informative.
Axillary flowers with five petals, an involucel of usually 8–9 bractlets, long exserted staminal column, ten style branches and capitate stigmas.
The fruit is an erect fleshy schizocarpic berry made of five indehiscent mericarps, not a dry capsule typical of many Hibiscus.
shared_genus_recognition.learning_warning: Do not mistake the exposed long staminal column for the style alone; identify the anthers along the column and distinct stigmatic branches at its tip.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: open flower and view beneath calyx
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Verify 5 rolled petals plus 8–9 involucellar bractlets, projecting staminal column and stigmas: Malvaviscus.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: several mature leaves, upper and lower, with young stem at node
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Consistently broad deeply cordate three-lobed leaves with dense stellate velvety hairs favor var. drummondii.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: mature leaf series on a noncultivated or garden specimen
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Mostly unlobed/shallow lobes, elongate blades and rounded bases suggest var. arboreus or another ornamental form; do not force local-variety name.
Confirm fleshy red five-part fruit. Dense root-derived colonizing stems can support var. drummondii, but do not excavate for ID.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: only parent-level photo/record or ornamental provenance
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Retain M. arboreus sensu lato and flag variety unresolved. Do not automatically install parent as second canonical species.

scientific_cautions: The Sheet's two source names are a broad parent and a particular variety; there is one separate local canonical infraspecific learner concept, not two species to install.
Native local var. drummondii is not equivalent to horticultural Malvaviscus arboreus parent without characters and source context.
FNA states var. arboreus appears introduced/rarely cultivated in the US; treat it as nonlocal comparison, not confirmed target-zone native.

Malvaviscus penduliflorus is a more robust planted look-alike with long drooping flowers and stamens often not fully protruding; verify identification and wild status instead of mistaking it for local Turk's cap.
Staminal column and style are different structures; use flower macro labels with individual stamens, anthers, style branches, stigmas.
Some cultivated forms change red/yellow flower appearance; color or bloom season alone cannot certify var. drummondii.
Don't convert county-native PASS or exact variety identification from a video caption alone; preserve the existing canonical decision and evidence.

local_lookalike_routing.separator: Many Hibiscus open their five petals broadly and typically develop drier capsules; compare unopened/fresh flower and mature fruit, epicalyx arrangement and staminal column.
Larger drooping flowers, often 7 cm, column not fully exserted, often fruitless in cultivation; compare fresh flower pose and mature fruit.
Mostly unlobed/weakly lobed, longer-than-wide leaves with rounded base and non-clonal growth, versus drummondii's broad deeply cordate three-lobed foliage.

local_lookalike_routing.taxon: Pavonia spp. and other local mallows
local_lookalike_routing.separator: Check rolled tube-like 5 petals, conspicuously protruding column and fleshy five-mericarp fruit rather than a generic mallow resemblance.

8–9 involucellar bractlets outside 5 true calyx lobes; arrow and count each structure

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: matched mature leaf and petiole/stem hairs
diagnostic_photo_requirements.target: var. drummondii vs var. arboreus comparison
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: three broad lobes/cordate base/velvety stellate hairs versus variable longer unlobed leaves and less velvety hairs
mature red fruit, five individual fleshy mericarps, not dry Hibiscus capsule
several natural stems from colony and mature leaf series, no digging
pendulous large flower and partially enclosed stamens versus local upright furled flower
